events.title: Martin Luther Stands Before the Diet of Worms
events.description: On the second day of his hearing before the Holy Roman Empire's assembly at Worms, Martin Luther was pressed to take back his writings. He refused to do so.
events.significance: His defiance set the Protestant Reformation on an irreversible course and permanently split Western Christianity.

events.title: Paul Revere's Midnight Ride
events.description: On the night of April 18, Paul Revere and other riders raced through the Massachusetts countryside. They warned colonists that British troops were on the move toward Lexington and Concord.
events.significance: The warning let militias gather, and the next morning's clashes at Lexington and Concord opened the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Great San Francisco Earthquake
events.description: An earthquake of an estimated magnitude of 7.9 struck San Francisco. Fires then raged through the city and destroyed much of it. At least 3,000 people died, and more than half of the population lost their homes.
events.significance: It was one of the worst natural disasters in U.S. history. It reshaped the city and influenced modern earthquake science and building practices.

events.title: Bandung Conference Opens
events.description: Twenty-nine nations from Asia and Africa gathered in Bandung, Indonesia, for the first large Asian-African Conference.
events.significance: The meeting gave newly independent and developing countries a shared voice. It helped lay the groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement during the Cold War.
